title: PowerPoint for Windows: create a presentation with Copilot from PowerPoint Home
summary: Hold: the connected-experiences control links to a Cloud Policy overview that does not document the named setting. The route and registry setting are supported across the cited Microsoft pages, but the control link must point to the setting's documentation. The policy-precedence comparison also needs to retain the overview's Windows Server qualification.

claims.claim: Microsoft lists the PowerPoint Home feature for Mac under roadmap item 560536.
claims.quote: "id": 560536; "description": "You can now create a presentation with Copilot in PowerPoint straight from the PowerPoint Home in file menu."; "platforms": ["Mac"]

claims.claim: Microsoft lists presentation creation directly from the PowerPoint web app under roadmap item 560537.
claims.quote: "id": 560537; "description": "You can now create a presentation with Copilot in PowerPoint just as you open the PowerPoint web app."; "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: The 22 July 2025 release notes already describe creating presentations from PowerPoint's Windows start or File menus.
claims.quote:
## July 22, 2025
Create a presentation with Microsoft 365 Copilot from menus [Windows]
You can quickly begin a new presentation using Microsoft 365 Copilot from the PowerPoint start menu or file menu.

claims.claim: Creating presentations from prompts is an existing Copilot capability in PowerPoint.
claims.quote: PowerPoint: Create presentations from prompts or existing content, summarize presentations or edit presentations (add images, apply deck-wide formatting changes)

claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot accesses content and context through Microsoft Graph.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot accesses content and context through Microsoft Graph.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Security & identity
claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot presents only data each individual can access, using existing Microsoft 365 data-access controls.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot presents only data that each individual can access using the same underlying controls for data access used in other Microsoft 365 services.

claims.claim: Prompts and responses are covered by Enterprise Data Protection when users sign in with Microsoft Entra accounts.
claims.quote: Copilot Chat (Basic), Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic), and Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) are protected by Enterprise Data Protection (EDP) when you sign in with Microsoft Entra accounts. With EDP, prompts and responses are protected

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Copilot provides presentation drafts for users to review rather than fully automating the task.
claims.quote: Our Microsoft Copilot capabilities provide useful drafts and summaries to help you achieve more while giving you a chance to review the generated AI rather than fully automating these tasks.

claims.claim: The supplied notice does not specify what source content the Home workflow can draw on beyond a prompt.
claims.quote:
Users will find a new option on PowerPoint Home (File menu) to create a presentation using Copilot.
Existing Microsoft 365 and Copilot policies are respected; no admin configuration changes are required.

claims.claim: Nothing in MC1311974 describes Copilot acting outside the new presentation file.
claims.quote: enabling presentation creation powered by Copilot directly from PowerPoint Home in the File menu. This update reduces friction at the start of the workflow, helping users move from idea to first draft faster without needing to open a new file.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot is now named Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot is now named Microsoft Copilot, and Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat is now named Microsoft Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) is an add-on licensed full experience in Word, Excel, PowerPoint and OneNote.
claims.quote: You have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license with access to the full experience of Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot is also available with Microsoft 365 E7.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot is available with Microsoft 365 E7 or as an add-on for eligible commercial, US Government, and education subscription plans.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) users have in-app Copilot access without the Copilot add-on.
claims.quote: You don't have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license but can use Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) includes creating PowerPoint presentations from prompts or existing content.
claims.quote:
Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) license and experience
In-app features you can use:
PowerPoint: Create presentations from prompts or existing content, summarize presentations or edit presentations

claims.claim: Some Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) features are subject to fair use limits.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) refers to users without the Copilot add-on license, but who have access to Copilot capabilities inside apps (for example, Word or Excel). It doesn't include full chat integration. Some features are subject to fair use limits.

claims.quote: Searched: "PowerPoint Home" "Windows" "Basic" "Copilot"; "PowerPoint Home" "Copilot" "Basic" license. Read Copilot overview, license options and release-note excerpts; Basic/Premium Home availability found only for the separate web feature.

claims.claim: No separate price for this PowerPoint Home option is published.
claims.quote: Searched: "PowerPoint" "presentation" "Copilot" "price" "meter" "Home"; PowerPoint Home Copilot price meter spending policy presentation creation. Read Copilot overview, license options and presentation release-note excerpts; no option-specific price stated.

claims.claim: No separate meter for this PowerPoint Home option is published.
claims.quote: Searched: "PowerPoint" "presentation" "Copilot" "price" "meter" "Home"; PowerPoint Home Copilot price meter spending policy presentation creation. Read Copilot overview, license options and release-note excerpts; no meter specific to this entry point stated.

claims.claim: No spending control specific to this PowerPoint Home option is published.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Home Copilot price meter spending policy presentation creation; PowerPoint Home create presentation Copilot 560694 Basic users policy hide entry point price meter spending control. Read Copilot overview and license options; no entry-point spending control stated.

claims.claim: The Cloud Policy overview documents the control at Customization > Policy Management > Create > Choose the scope > Configure Settings > Allow the use of connected experiences in Office that analyze content.
claims.quote: Searched: named analyze-content policy with "Configure Settings" "Cloud Policy". Read Cloud Policy overview and manage-privacy-controls. The route is supported jointly, but the linked overview does not name or document the setting at its last step.
claims.fix: Keep the path, but replace controls[0].ui.docs and the corresponding table link with https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-apps/privacy/manage-privacy-controls#policy-setting-for-connected-experiences-that-analyze-your-content. That page documents the setting and its availability through Cloud Policy; retain the Cloud Policy overview in sources for the route into the wizard.

claims.claim: Setting usercontentdisabled to DWORD 2 under HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Policies\Microsoft\office\16.0\common\privacy disables the analyze-content policy.
claims.quote:
Allow the use of connected experiences in Office that analyze content | UserContentDisabled | 1=Enabled 2=Disabled
[HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Policies\Microsoft\office\16.0\common\privacy]
"usercontentdisabled"=dword:00000001

claims.where: controls[0].governs; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Turning off connected experiences that analyze content makes Copilot unavailable in PowerPoint and the other listed Office apps on current Windows, Mac, iOS and Android versions.
claims.quote:
Microsoft Copilot features won't be available to your users in the following apps:
- Excel
- OneNote
- Outlook
- PowerPoint
- Word
This applies to when you're running the most current version of these apps on Windows, Mac, iOS, or Android devices.

claims.claim: The analyze-content policy controls the whole category of connected experiences, not only Copilot.
claims.quote: You can use the Allow the use of connected experiences in Office that analyze content policy setting to control whether these types of connected experiences are available to your users.

claims.claim: Office Apps Administrator is the recommended role for Cloud Policy.
claims.quote: Office Apps Administrator (Recommended) | This role can manage Office apps cloud services, including policy and settings management

claims.claim: The licence-assignment control is in Microsoft 365 admin center at Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
claims.quote: go to the Users > Active users page. Select the row of the user ... In the right pane, select Licenses and Apps. Expand the Licenses section, select the boxes for the licenses that you want to assign

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns the chosen product licence.
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: Licence assignment requires at least License Administrator or User Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: Cloud Policy settings normally apply when Office apps restart.
claims.quote: Policies from Cloud Policy are applied only when the Office app is restarted. The behavior is the same as with Group Policy.

claims.claim: Some privacy-control policies apply without restarting Office apps.
claims.quote: Some policies related to privacy controls will apply without restarting any Office apps.

claims.claim: The Cloud Policy overview says Cloud Policy takes precedence over Group Policy.
claims.quote: policy settings implemented by using Cloud Policy take precedence over policy settings implemented by using Group Policy on Windows Server
claims.fix: Replace the precedence comparison with: "The Cloud Policy overview says Cloud Policy takes precedence over Group Policy on Windows Server; Microsoft's sensitive-and-regulated-customer guidance says Group Policy takes precedence for Win32 Office apps where both are in use and advises keeping the policies aligned." Retain both existing citations.

claims.claim: The sensitive-and-regulated-customer guidance says Group Policy takes precedence for Win32 Office apps where both policy mechanisms are used.
claims.quote: Rich client Office applications (Win32 apps) are controlled by both Group Policy and Cloud Policy, with Group Policy taking precedence where both are in use.

claims.claim: Microsoft's sensitive-and-regulated-customer guidance advises keeping Group Policy and Cloud Policy aligned.
claims.quote: For organizations that use a combination of Group Policy and Cloud Policy, keep these policies aligned to avoid confusion.

claims.claim: Removing the Microsoft Copilot add-on removes access to its licensed experience as a whole, not just the PowerPoint Home option.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Copilot user subscription license ... contains eight separate components ... If you remove the license from a user, the user loses access to Copilot.
